cases.scenario: User asks for total conversions across four advertising and analytics platforms. No shared identity key exists across them.
pass_if: The summed figure appears first, before any caveat
Every component is listed with how that platform counts: date basis, window, model
The direction of the error is named as overstating
The magnitude is stated as unquantified without a shared key, with no invented percentage
Warehouse deduplication on a shared key is named as the better number
A holdout or geo test is named as the route to a causal number
The output states when the rough figure is fine
fail_if: The total is withheld
The user is asked to acknowledge a warning before receiving the total
An overlap percentage is stated without a shared key to measure it
The total ships with no annotation
Caveats appear above the number

cases.scenario: Campaign-level conversion rows from the professional network are summed to an account total. The default attribution basis counts once per campaign.
pass_if: Identifies that the default basis counts a conversion once per campaign
States that summing campaign rows double-counts people touched by several campaigns, by design
Distinguishes this from cross-platform overlap as a separate, additional source of overstatement
Offers the account-level query as the correct route to an account total
fail_if: Reports the campaign sum as the account total with no disclosure
Attributes the discrepancy to a tracking problem
Claims the other platforms have the same behaviour

cases.scenario: Three ad platforms are compared. All three support a 7-day click window. Their defaults are 30, 7 and 30 days.
pass_if: Re-queries all three at a 7-day click window and labels that the comparable series
Retains the platform-default numbers as a separate labelled series
Presents both
Names the residuals normalisation did not fix: date basis, event set, per-campaign counting, modelled components
fail_if: Presents only the normalised series
Presents only the platform-default series
Claims the normalised series is fully comparable
Silently picks one series without labelling it

cases.scenario: A 30-day before-and-after comparison where the earlier window has 30 days of data and the later has 22, because of a tracking outage.
pass_if: Computes and displays covered-day counts on both sides
States that equal calendar windows do not mean equal coverage here
Uses an observed-day rate, or suppresses the raw comparison and says why
Names the coverage gap rather than reporting the shortfall as a decline
fail_if: Reports the difference as a performance change
Compares the raw totals without a coverage check
Extrapolates the 22 days to 30 without labelling the result as estimated

cases.scenario: A CRM influence model reports 4.2M marketing-sourced pipeline. The marketing platform's own attribution reports 6.8M. The user asks which is correct.
pass_if: States that both are real and they answer different questions
Names the mechanism of each: one campaign per opportunity against credit to every touching campaign
Names the direction of each figure's bias
Names the defensible alternative: a multi-touch model over an assembled journey, credit summing to one per opportunity
Does not iterate attempting to reconcile them to a single figure
fail_if: Declares one figure correct and the other wrong without stating the definitions
Attempts to reconcile the two to a single number
Averages them
Reports the discrepancy as a data quality defect

cases.scenario: A period-over-period comparison is being generated for repeated use. The prior window could be written as literal dates or derived per row.
pass_if: Derives the comparison endpoints from each row's own event date
Does not write literal date boundaries into a reusable query
States that a hardcoded endpoint is correct on the authoring day and silently wrong after
fail_if: Writes literal date boundaries into a query intended for repeated use
Relies on the current date being the authoring date

cases.scenario: An in-house qualified-lead definition and a platform metric of the same name are about to be charted on one axis.
pass_if: Refuses the shared axis without both denominators and definitions labelled
Names the in-house metric distinctly from the vendor metric
States explicitly that the two are not comparable despite the shared name
Still charts both, separately labelled, rather than dropping one
fail_if: Charts both on one axis under the shared name
Drops one series instead of labelling both
Treats the name match as evidence of a definition match
